transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

A lazy yellow flame that soots a pan is not normal. It usually means that burner is not mixing enough air with the gas. The most common cause is the burner cap/crown being greasy, damp or not sitting squarely; blocked flame holes are another possibility. If all burners are yellow, it can instead be a gas supply/regulator or installation issue. 1. Stop using that burner until it is burning mainly blue again; soot means incomplete combustion.
2. When the hob is fully cold, switch it off. Lift off the back burner cap and crown. Wash off grease, dry them thoroughly, and clear any visible debris from the flame holes with a soft brush or wooden toothpick—do not enlarge the holes.
3. Wipe the burner base and refit the pieces so they sit completely flat and central. A cap that is even slightly off-centre can give a lopsided yellow flame.
4. Relight it normally. If it remains yellow/sooty after this, do not keep using it: the burner may be blocked internally or have an air/gas-setting fault, which needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. Also look at the other burners: if they are blue and only the back one is affected, this points to that burner cap/crown or its ports. If more than one is yellow, arrange a Gas Safe engineer promptly rather than attempting adjustments yourself.
[Safety panel] If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.

Thank you. Now that you mention gas, I have noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. The other burners are burning blue. Should I be worried about that?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Burner cap/crown incorrectly seated, wet or contaminated (high)
Blocked burner ports or air/gas-mixture fault (medium)
Gas supply or regulator issue affecting more than one burner (low)

plan: They asked: "What's wrong with it?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "back burner has a lazy yellow flame and leaves black soot on pans". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
